turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_constrained_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_constrained_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Both of these hard constraints apply to every candidate:
  1. molybdenum content at most 3.21 wt%;
  2. alloying cost index Σ (price_e × wt%_e) at most 450, using the prices in USD/kg: C 0.5, Mn 2, Si 2.2, Cr 9, Ni 17, Mo 25, V 30, Nb 45, Co 33, Al 2.4, Ti 12, Cu 9.
A candidate that violates either constraint is worth zero, so picking one wastes a slot. Using the training data, predict which FEASIBLE candidates have the HIGHEST yield strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training data show that the highest yield strengths (typically 2000–2400 MPa) occur for alloys that combine substantial Co (approximately 4–7 wt%) with moderate Ni, Mo and precipitation-forming additions (V, Nb, Ti), processed by quench-and-temper or solution-age treatments. Wrought and cast routes outperform AM; annealing produces distinctly lower strengths. Aging temperatures of 480–650 °C and solutionizing temperatures above ~1050 °C are favorable. These empirical patterns, together with the two hard constraints, immediately eliminate every candidate whose Mo exceeds 3.21 wt% or whose alloying-cost index exceeds 450.

Among the remaining feasible recipes the five that best match the high-strength training cluster (and therefore receive the highest predicted strengths) are:

- c092 (Co 6.75, Mo 2.60, V+Nb 1.07, quench-temper, aging 552 °C)
- c007 (Co 5.26, high Ni+Ti+Nb, quench-temper, wrought)
- c044 (Co 4.72, Ni+Mo+Nb, quench-temper, high solutionizing temperature)
- c042 (Co 3.34, Ni+Mo+V, solution-aged at the peak-aging temperature 509 °C)
- c029 (Co 4.86, Ni+V+Ti, quenched, wrought)

All five satisfy both constraints and lie closest, in both composition and processing, to the strongest observed training examples.

Final: c092, c007, c044, c042, c029
